question: A developer wants Claude to have awareness of a project's coding conventions when answering questions in a dedicated 'Backend Refactor' project. Which action correctly places that context so it applies across all chats in the project?
options: A) Star the coding convention files in a personal favorites list to make them available across project chats.
B) Ask Claude to memorize the coding conventions in a single chat to persist across project chats.
C) Rename each new chat to include the word 'conventions' so Claude infers the context across chats.
D) Upload the convention docs to the project's knowledge base with the '+' button on the main page.
correct_answers: D) Upload the convention docs to the project's knowledge base with the '+' button on the main page.
explanations: Incorrect. A personal favorites list is a user-specific bookmarking feature and does not inject content into Claude's context. Project knowledge base is the proper mechanism for providing shared documents across chats.
Incorrect. Memorization within a single chat does not persist to other chats. To share context across all project chats, you must upload the material to the project's knowledge base.
Incorrect. Chat names are only labels and do not convey document content or give Claude awareness of conventions. Only the project knowledge base can provide persistent context across chats.

Correct. Uploading documents to the project's knowledge base with the '+' button injects them as context across all chats. This ensures Claude always has access to the coding conventions when answering in the 'Backend Refactor' project.
